title: Superside vs. OLIVER, The Brandtech Group's in-house agency
summary: Superside vs OLIVER, the in-house agency that's part of The Brandtech Group. Compare an embedded agency model with Superside's flexible plans to find the right fit.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


OLIVER agency builds and runs marketing teams inside client organizations, while Superside pairs AI-native experts with AI systems through a flexible subscription. The embedded model wins on daily immersion and institutional knowledge, and Superside wins on variable demand, specialist range and brand knowledge held in a system. Many enterprises end up using both, so match each model to the work it does best.


**OLIVER, part of The Brandtech Group, and Superside both help enterprise marketing teams keep pace with relentless demand for creative.** But they do it in very different ways. OLIVER takes an embedded approach. It designs, builds and runs marketing organizations inside the brands it works with.


**Superside, the world's largest AI-native creative agency** , pairs[AI-native experts](https://www.superside.com/our-creative-talent) with AI systems through[a single platform](https://www.superside.com/our-technology) . You choose a Flex plan that scales with your workload or a Dedicated team that stays the same every month.


So your choice depends on how you want to organize creative support: a team embedded inside your organization or one you access through a subscription.


This article compares the two models across[creative services](https://www.superside.com/blog/benefits-of-creative-services) , flexibility, pricing, AI and brand knowledge, and is open about where each one wins. Throughout, we label claims about OLIVER as either verified ( *press releases and trade coverage* ) or OLIVER's own description of itself.


## How in-housing is changing creative production


**In-house agencies have moved from the exception to the rule.** The Association of National Advertisers'[May 2023 in-house agency study](https://www.ana.net/content/show/id/79185) found that **82% of members have an in-house agency, up from 78% in 2018.**


That doesn't always mean a fully staffed creative department. The ANA's definition covers any department, group or even a single person handling work an external agency would typically do.


And here's the telling part: **92% of those organizations still work with external agencies too.** Even strong internal teams need extra skills or support.


**AI is accelerating the shift** . In a[November 2025 study by the WFA and MediaSense](https://wfanet.org/knowledge/item/2025/11/04/how-ai-is-changing-in-house-agencies) , based on a survey and interviews with 30 global in-house agency leaders, 93% said they plan to invest further in AI in the next 12 to 24 months. Yet only 12% were already fully integrating it.


Brands also expect to bring more work inside. Survey data fielded by NewtonX for[Adweek](https://www.adweek.com/agencies/as-ai-fuels-in-housing-surge-agency-execs-take-the-entrepreneurial-path/) found that 32% of brands expect to handle nearly all creative in-house within 12 months, and another 23% expect to bring at least half in-house. The full article is paywalled, so treat those figures as directional.


Together, these findings point to a clear pattern. Many top brands keep brand knowledge close through internal teams, then bring in outside partners for specialist skills and busy periods. OLIVER and Superside are two very different ways to fill that outside role.

## OLIVER vs Superside: Two models side by side


**The biggest difference is how the work gets done.** OLIVER builds a marketing team inside your business. Superside gives you flexible access to AI-native experts and AI systems through a subscription.


The second difference is transparency. OLIVER doesn't publish pricing or standard terms, so its engagements are set case by case.[Superside's pricing](https://www.superside.com/pricing) is public: subscriptions start at a $15,000 monthly minimum on an annual term, plus a $1,000 monthly software fee, and unused Flex budget rolls over for up to three months.

## Where OLIVER's embedded model wins


**Some of the world's biggest brands choose embedded teams for good reason.** For the right kind of work, having people inside your business is hard to beat.


### Daily immersion


An embedded team is part of the business. It hears the conversations, joins the meetings and picks up the context that even a good[creative brief](https://www.superside.com/blog/creative-briefs-production) can miss.


### Single-brand focus


An embedded team built around your brand goes deeper on it over time, which can lead to more consistent work.


### Institutional knowledge


Over time, the team learns which decisions were made and why. That context is especially valuable on complex, long-running work.


### On-site collaboration


Being there means picking up feedback that never makes it into a formal brief. A passing comment that a landing page feels off can reach the team straight away.


**The nutshell:** If deep brand immersion and daily collaboration are your top priorities, an embedded model like OLIVER's makes sense. The trade-off is flexibility, because you're committing to a team sized for today's needs.


## Where Superside's flexible model wins


Superside's model brings a different set of strengths. **It's the better fit when:**


### Demand is variable


If your creative volume spikes for launches and drops afterward, a fixed team can leave you over- or under-resourced. Superside's Flex plan scales with your workload, and unused budget rolls over for up to three months.


Our guide to[creative bandwidth](https://www.superside.com/blog/capacity-and-bandwidth) explains why that matters more than you might expect.


### You need specialist range


A single team can only cover so many skills, and enterprise creative needs now go well beyond static graphics.


With Superside, you work with specialists across motion and video, web and landing page design, ad creative, branding, presentations and more, with project management included. All of our[creative services](https://www.superside.com/design-services) sit with one partner.


### You want a faster, structured start


Onboarding is included in every Superside plan, with your first project landing within the first few weeks. Teams that want a faster ramp-up can add Quick Start, a three-week engagement that configures Brand Brain, trains stakeholders and hands off a working playbook.


### You'd rather not lock budget into a fixed team


Enterprise priorities change. Superside plans run on an annual term, but within it you can shift your Flex budget across formats and scope month to month, without rebuilding a team.


### AI needs to be part of the work


AI is no longer a novelty. The difference is between partners that add AI on top and those that build it into how creative gets made.


Superside pairs AI-native experts with[AI systems](https://www.superside.com/ai-excellence) that connect brand context, briefing and[creative quality control](https://www.superside.com/blog/ai-creative-quality-control) . The result is standout, on-brand creative that measurably performs, with real creatives behind every output.


## The costs neither proposal shows


**Whatever the model, creative support costs more than the monthly fee.**


Look closely at these costs and risks as you compare proposals:


Cost or risk Embedded agency Creative subscription


Getting started Building and staffing a team takes time An existing team and platform can shorten setup


Quiet periods Committed staffing costs can leave the team underused Budget rollover can absorb fluctuations


Scope changes May require changes to staffing, fees or the contract Budget can move across types of work within the plan


Key-person turnover Continuity depends on documentation and handover Shared brand systems help preserve knowledge across team changes


Specialist skills May require extra hires or outside support A broader specialist pool reduces the need for more vendors


Ending the relationship Contract obligations and an operational handover Contract terms, notice periods and transition still apply


Notice how an embedded team's biggest strength can also be its biggest risk. Its core asset is people who know your brand deeply, and when they leave, much of that knowledge can leave with them.


So whichever provider you consider, ask: What happens to everything your team has learned about our brand when people leave?


The other cost is structural. A team sized for your busiest quarter is over-resourced for the other three, and a team sized for an average quarter is stretched at peak. A flexible partner can cover the peaks without carrying a larger team year-round.


## What to ask both partners


**Put the same questions to every provider on your shortlist:**


- **What if our volume doubles for a quarter?** Ask how they'd scale up, how quickly and at what cost.
- **What if demand halves?** Check which costs stay fixed and whether unused budget rolls over.
- **How do you preserve brand knowledge?** Ask how guidelines, feedback and past decisions are captured when people change. Superside uses[Brand Brain](https://www.superside.com/brandbrain) to retain and build on that context.
- **When can work start, and what does setup cost?** Separate kickoff, your first brief and your first finished creative.
- **How does AI improve the work?** Ask to see workflows, quality controls and evidence of better efficiency or[creative performance](https://www.superside.com/blog/what-is-creative-performance) .
- **What does a scope change involve?** Check fees, approval steps and effects on timelines.
- **Can we see full pricing and contract terms?** Compare minimum commitments, what's included, extra charges and exit terms.

## How to run the evaluation


Structure the comparison around your own demand rather than the pitches. **Follow these steps:**


### 1. Map your demand before you meet anyone


Separate ongoing work from seasonal peaks and occasional specialist projects. Which tasks need daily collaboration and deep business knowledge? Where do you mainly need extra hands or skills?


Steady work that needs close involvement in daily decisions may favor an embedded team. Fluctuating volume and varied specialist needs may favor a flexible subscription.


### 2. Test the AI claim specifically


Most agencies now use AI in some form. Ask which workflows use it, who's trained to direct it and how outputs are checked. Then ask for evidence of gains in speed, brand consistency and creative performance.


### 3. Model the full three years


Compare the total cost over three years: setup, ongoing fees, unused budget in quiet periods, a couple of scope changes and ending the contract.


Two options that cost about the same in year one can look very different once your needs change.


### 4. Check what happens when people change


For an embedded team, ask how it keeps brand knowledge and quality when someone leaves. For a flexible partner, ask how specialists learn your brand and stay consistent when different people pick up projects.


In both cases, look for clear documentation, handover processes and quality checks that don't depend on any one person.


**Side note:** Embedded and flexible agencies aren't your only options. You can also compare[Superside vs. freelancers](https://www.superside.com/compare-superside-vs-freelancers) ,[Superside vs. a traditional agency](https://www.superside.com/compare-superside-vs-agency) or[Superside vs. in-house hiring](https://www.superside.com/compare-superside-vs-inhouse) .


## Why many enterprises use more than one model


**Remember the ANA finding: 92% of organizations with an in-house agency still work with external agencies.** Even the biggest brands rarely choose one creative model for everything.


Different work calls for different support. An embedded team makes sense where daily collaboration matters most. A flexible partner becomes crucial when you need more output, new formats or specialist skills fast.


Getting the right mix isn't just an[enterprise creative](https://www.superside.com/blog/enterprise-creative-agency) challenge, either. Many growth-stage companies face the same pressure as demand climbs.

## Superside vs. OLIVER: Which model suits your team?


**If your creative demand is steady and your brand needs daily attention from people inside the business, OLIVER's embedded model makes sense.** You get a team that knows your business and works alongside you every day.


If your demand changes often, **Superside gives you more flexibility** . You can bring in specialists for everything from social and ad creative to brand strategy, video and presentation design, without building those skills into a fixed team. Our pricing is public, so it's easier to understand the investment upfront.


For many enterprise and growth-stage teams, the answer is both. Use embedded talent where daily collaboration matters and flexible support where you need extra skills or scale. The key is to match the model to the work.
